reviews.current_ambiguity: Global functoriality ranges over different groups and L-group homomorphisms; there is no single finite verification obligation.
reviews.draft_scope: Choose a specific pair of reductive groups over a named number field class, a single L-group map, and the associated cuspidal automorphic transfer with local/global hypotheses; do not select a particular lift without comparing recent solved cases.
open_questions: Which named transfer remains open after recent special-case advances?
Does the theorem target existence alone or cuspidality and characterization at ramified places?
Which restricted transfer has a specialist-defined proof obligation?
reviews.promotion_barrier: The cited 2026 symmetric-power result covers important Hilbert modular cases; select a *different demonstrably open residue* before changing M017.

reviews.current_ambiguity: Weak cosmic censorship uses genericity and nakedness conditions that depend on matter model, asymptotics, regularity and initial-data topology.
reviews.draft_scope: For one fixed Einstein evolution model and a specified class of asymptotically flat Cauchy data, formulate the precise genericity topology, maximal-development assumptions, completeness of future null infinity, and visibility criterion; this is a scope template, not a new accepted conjecture.
open_questions: Which data class, matter model and norm define admissible perturbations?
Is genericity openness, density, residuality or full measure in a stated topology?
Does the chosen statement concern weak censorship at null infinity rather than strong censorship at a Cauchy horizon?
reviews.promotion_barrier: Do not use results about strong cosmic censorship or a provisional near-Kerr problem list as evidence that this full weak censorship scope is solved or open.

reviews.current_ambiguity: The registry omits dimension, surface, exponents, and whether endpoint and broad versus diagonal extension estimates are included.
reviews.draft_scope: Distinguish (a) Fourier extension from smooth positively curved surfaces in R^3 in the diagonal p-to-p range, (b) bounded-data extension in R^3, and (c) the sharp sphere restriction/extension program in arbitrary dimensions with explicit p and q and endpoint conventions.
open_questions: Which of the distinct Euclidean extension inequalities should own M056?
What exponent and endpoint ranges remain after 2026 diagonal and bounded-data manuscript claims?
Are both higher-dimensional cases and endpoints intended or is a single finite-dimensional statement preferable?
reviews.promotion_barrier: The 2026 manuscript claims an R^3 diagonal nonendpoint result, not an audited resolution of every dimension/exponent/endpoint case.

reviews.current_ambiguity: A planar first-passage fluctuation exponent needs an edge-weight law, point-to-point observable, and asymptotic interpretation; exactly solvable last-passage models are not the same question.
reviews.draft_scope: As a candidate precise target: on nearest-neighbor Z^2 with independent rate-one exponential nonnegative edge passage times, let T_n be the minimal total edge weight from the origin to (n,0); ask whether Var(T_n) = n^(2/3+o(1)) as n tends to infinity.
open_questions: Does the exponent claim hold for point-to-point passage time along the coordinate axis under this law?
Should the target concern a broader class of continuous weight laws or this specific benchmark model?
Which prior variance bounds and exact finite-scale simulation results apply to this model?
reviews.promotion_barrier: The cited article discusses KPZ predictions and solvable *last*-passage benchmarks. It is not a contemporary primary verification that this specific FPP variance statement remains open.

reviews.current_ambiguity: The 3D Ising conjecture conflates field existence, non-Gaussianity, conformal covariance, universality and possible regularity conditions.
reviews.draft_scope: Choose critical nearest-neighbor Ising on the cubic lattice in dimension three and identify a correctly normalized magnetization distribution, a named scaling topology, and finite-dimensional correlation/covariance properties; only then formulate non-Gaussian conformal covariance as an exact theorem.
open_questions: Which field observable and normalization are intended: spin/magnetization, energy, or both?
In what space/topology is tightness and scaling convergence claimed?
Which conformal transformations and boundary conditions are part of the target?
reviews.promotion_barrier: A 2025 review provides context about the Ising frontier but is not a specialist verification of the chosen exact 3D scaling-limit claim.
